patch.summary: Capsule tiers are a quota ladder rather than a feature narrative. Contact, pipeline, and custom-field limits scale strictly by plan tier. Published rungs: Free ($0/mo) · Starter ($18/seat/mo billed annually) · Growth ($36/seat/mo billed annually) · Advanced ($54/seat/mo billed annually) · Ultimate ($72/seat/mo billed annually). Which means you can pick your tier arithmetically: check contacts, pipelines, custom fields, and users against each rung, and stop at the first one that holds all four. Only one capability question sits on top of that: Workflow automations and advanced reporting start at Growth; enrichment at Advanced.

seo.title: Capsule Plans: A Quota Ladder, Not a Feature Story
seo.description: Pick a Capsule tier by checking four quotas — contacts, pipelines, custom fields, users — then one capability question. Workflow automations and advanced reporting start at Growth; enrichment at Advanced.

sections.heading: Four numbers, checked in order
sections.body: Contact, pipeline, and custom-field limits scale strictly by plan tier. So write your four numbers down before you look at any rung: how many contacts you will actually keep, how many pipelines you genuinely run, how many custom fields your reports depend on, and how many people need a login. Then walk up the ladder and stop at the first rung that holds all four. This takes five minutes and is more reliable than comparing feature bullets, because the constraint that will bite you is almost always a quota rather than a missing feature. The free rung is a real starting point for a very small team, but its user and contact caps are tight enough that most teams pass it inside a year.

sections.heading: The one capability step that is worth planning for
sections.body: Workflow automations and advanced reporting start at Growth; enrichment at Advanced. That is the single place where the ladder stops being about volume and starts being about what the software does for you. The pricing threshold to watch, then, is the point where you want the system to do something on a schedule instead of a person doing it on a Tuesday — a task created automatically when a deal changes stage, for instance. You gain that automation at the cost of a higher per-seat rate across your whole team, so it is worth naming the specific repeated action first; a vague desire for automation does not survive that arithmetic.

sections.heading: What this deliberately is not
sections.body: Not a marketing automation or sales-engagement suite — email templates ≠ full campaign platform. That boundary is the reason the tiers stay legible: you are buying a well-kept contact and pipeline record, not a campaign platform wearing a CRM badge. Weak fit if your plan for next quarter is behavioural email journeys — you would be pairing this with a dedicated sending tool anyway, so budget for both rather than expecting one to become the other. Migration in is usually simple because the data model is small; migration out later is likewise cheap, which is a genuine and underrated advantage when you are not yet sure what you will need.
sections.tip: Count custom fields honestly — the reports you already rely on define that number.

blocks.heading: Write the four numbers before you open the pricing page
blocks.body: Contacts you will keep, pipelines you run, custom fields your reports read, people who need logins. Four numbers on one line. Doing this first stops you from being sold a rung by a feature list, because the ladder is genuinely built around these quotas and nothing else moves as reliably.

blocks.heading: Name the repeated action you want the system to take
blocks.body: "Create a follow-up task whenever a deal enters negotiation" is a specification. "Better automation" is not. One named action justifies the rung where workflow automation begins; zero named actions means stay lower and revisit in a quarter with evidence.
blocks.tip: Write the automation as a sentence with a trigger and an action, or skip it.

blocks.heading: Decide where campaign email will live, and budget for it
blocks.body: Because this is deliberately not a campaign platform, your email programme needs a home. Choose the sending tool now and add its cost to the comparison. Buyers who skip this step compare a CRM-only price against an all-in-one price and reach a conclusion the numbers do not support.
